pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list: '— high' and '— low' labels, and none on normal items.
The 'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters and their order.
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong>.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The Set lookup in src/index.js is safe.
The 'AC-7' test asserts the exact messages for high, low and normal no-match, and 'No items yet.' in every view on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high. The 'AC-8' test checks it. The traffic worker passes the path, query included, to the app.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null or a string and is never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec's States table row 'No match' now has no exact-message check in the states test. The AC-7 test still checks the messages, so the gap is partly covered.
findings.fix: Restore expect(message(html)).toBe("No low-priority items.") in the 'No match' state test.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened an assertion (see the tests finding). The body also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', yet a later commit edited a test.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it in the PR body.

findings.what: The README does not mention that traffic/routes.json entries may now carry a query string, which is a changed rule in scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs. It also does not say that other priority values answer 400.
findings.fix: Add one line to the README traffic section saying routes may include a query string.

lenses.note: The change follows specs/item-priority.md. The traffic-check relaxation is needed for AC-8 and is disclosed in the PR.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and have named tests. The only gap is the loosened 'No match' state assertion.
The tests are mostly strong. The final commit weakened the 'No match' state assertion to toBeDefined(), which can never fail. I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
The README mentions the filter. The query-string route rule is not documented.
No defects found. Priority is validated against a Set and bound as a query parameter.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority is allowlisted, and the SQL is parameterised. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files, only the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and the PR names no screenshots.
There is no browser in this session and no preview. The only UI is plain server-rendered HTML.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims 'Tests loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' are false because of the last commit.
